newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rubber - Japan prices seen lower on currency concern.
newsitem.headline: Rubber - Japan prices seen lower on currency concern.

text.p: Japanese rubber futures prices are likely to drift lower next week, amid nervousness over a worsening currency crisis in Southeast Asia and speculation that Thailand will sell its rubber stocks, traders said.
A statement by the Indonesian central bank this week that it will no longer announce its daily intervention/conversion bands cast a shadow on an already bearish Tokyo rubber market, they said.

"Japanese rubber futures are likely to probe downside support at around 110 yen in the near-term, as prices in overseas markets and the offer prices of Thai benchmark rubber to Japan are expected to fall due to weaker currencies in Southeast Asia," a commodity broker said.
On the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM), benchmark January rubber ended the morning session lower at 115.1 yen per kg, against Thursday's close of 115.7 yen.
Benchmark January on the Kobe Rubber Exchange ended the morning session at 115.8 yen per kg, down from the previous day's close of 116.5 yen.

Market talk that the Thai government may sell its rubber stocks in an attempt to balance the budget to meet conditions set by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) for a bailout package, were also seen negative for the market.
"Concern that the Thai government may sell its stocks is likely to unnerve the market. Most buyers will remain sidelined," one trader said.
"The yen's weakness against the dollar failed to lift rubber prices by midday today, which disappointed market participants. This also shows how bearish market sentiment has become," he added.
Expectations that market players will be reluctant to take deliveries when the spot August contract expires on August 25 also dented sentiment, traders said.
"The quality August delivery rubber is expected to be poor and such expectations are pressuring the market, especially nearby months," an analyst at a commodity brokerage said.
"A modest technical rebound is likely next week, but unless the yen dives against the dollar, chances that rubber prices will fully recover are slim," he said.
Thai rubber to Japan was offered at 95.00 U.S. cents per kg on an FOB basis on Friday, unchanged compared with August 8.
In the local physical market, benchmark Thai rubber for large-lot end users was quoted at 122.00 yen per kg as of Friday, compared with 125.00 yen a week ago.
